items.q: In SMART objectives, what does the T stand for in the AQA specification?
items.why: The specification lists Specific, Measurable, Accountable, Realistic, Time specific.

items.q: What is the main benefit of limited liability for shareholders?
opts: They can only lose the money they invested, so their personal possessions are protected
items.why: Limited liability encourages people to invest because the risk to them is capped.

items.q: How do shareholders control a plc?
opts: By managing the business day to day
By voting on decisions, such as electing directors, at meetings like the AGM
items.why: Shareholders own the company and vote, usually one vote per share. Directors and managers run it day to day.

items.q: Which of these is a reason to buy shares?
opts: To receive dividends and possibly sell the shares later for more than you paid
To lend money that must be repaid with interest
items.why: Shareholders hope for dividends and a rise in the share price. Neither is guaranteed.

items.q: What is an ethical dilemma in business?
opts: A choice between two equally profitable options
A choice where the most profitable option may not be the morally right one
items.why: The specification mentions profit vs ethics as an example.

items.q: What is one advantage of secondary market research?
opts: It is usually quicker and cheaper to get than primary research
It is always up to date
It is collected for the business's exact purpose
items.why: Secondary data already exists, but it may be out of date or not quite fit what the business needs.

items.q: Which of these is quantitative data?
opts: 62% of customers would visit a shop
A customer's review explaining why they returned a product
Customers said the mugs feel 'lovely to hold'
items.why: Quantitative data is numerical. The others are qualitative.

items.q: How does a business decide what to put on the axes of a market map?
opts: It always uses sales and profit
It chooses two features that matter to customers, such as price and quality
It uses the Boston Matrix axes
items.why: The axes should reflect what customers care about when choosing between products.

items.q: What does return on marketing spend measure?
opts: The profit made from marketing compared with the amount spent on it
items.why: Return on marketing spend = profit from marketing activities ÷ marketing spend × 100.

items.q: What does an index number show?
opts: How a figure has changed compared with a base year, which is set at 100
A business's ranking in its market
items.why: An index of 120 means 20% higher than the base year.

items.q: When will cutting the price increase a business's revenue?
opts: When the product is an inferior good
items.why: With elastic demand, quantity rises by a larger percentage than price falls.

items.q: What YED would you expect for a supermarket's value own-label range?
items.why: Value ranges are often inferior goods: when incomes rise, some customers trade up to branded or premium products.

items.q: A sportswear brand targeting teenagers mainly uses TikTok rather than newspaper adverts. What is this an example of?
opts: Adapting the marketing mix for the target market
items.why: The promotion is chosen to reach the target market where they spend their time.

items.q: Growth in a market slows down. What is likely to happen to competition?
opts: It increases, because firms can only grow by taking customers from each other
items.why: In a slow-growing market, one firm's gain is usually another's loss, so rivalry tends to increase.

items.q: What usually happens to a product in the maturity stage?
opts: Sales are at or near their peak and growth slows
The product has not been launched
items.why: Many rivals are in the market by now, so the business may use extension strategies.

items.q: What is a star in the Boston Matrix?
opts: A product with a high share in a low-growth market
A product with a low share in a low-growth market
The best-selling product of all time
A product with a high market share in a high-growth market
items.why: Stars earn well but often need heavy spending to keep up with the growing market.

items.q: What is the main purpose of market research?
opts: To guarantee that a product will sell
To reduce the risk of business decisions by understanding customers and markets
items.why: Better information lowers risk, but it cannot remove it.

items.q: Marketing forecasts a big rise in sales. Which other function is most directly affected?
opts: None, marketing decisions only affect marketing
Operations, which may need more capacity, stock and staff
items.why: Marketing decisions affect operations, finance and HR. The specification calls this the interrelationship between functions.

items.q: What does brand awareness measure?
opts: How much customers like the product
The proportion of the target market who recognise or know the brand
items.why: Brand awareness is one of the marketing objectives in the specification.

items.q: What is discount pricing?
opts: Setting a high price at launch
Setting prices below rivals to attract price-sensitive customers
items.why: Discount pricing is a competition-based method. Businesses like Aldi and Lidl use it.
